name: Stratford Steel
old_description: We have worked with Stratford Steel Fabrication since 2017 on approximately 7 historical restoration projects and they have been great to work with.
about:
Stratford Steel Fabrication operates from Stratford, Connecticut. The company was founded in 2017, according to directory records, and draws on over 150 years of collective industry experience among its team. Ownership structure and founders are not publicly disclosed.

The shop specializes in custom ornamental metalwork, producing stairs, railings, canopies, and restoration components in steel, brass, aluminum, and stainless steel. All work — estimating, drafting, engineering, project management, fabrication, finishing, and installation — is performed in-house. Facility size, headcount, and annual volume are not published.

The firm serves architects, conservation and restoration firms, general contractors, and developers across the Tri-State area. Notable projects include a brass spiral staircase for a Gramercy penthouse, canopy fabrication for the Walker Hotel, restoration of 100-year-old railings at the Knickerbocker Club, stainless steel replacement parts for the Marcus Garvey Watchtower, a cantilevered stair in East Hampton, and a poolhouse canopy in Greenwich. Clients such as Jan Hird Pokorny Associates, Highline Construction Group, Legere Group, and trueEX Group have cited the company's turn-key capability and responsiveness.

Stratford Steel states its mission is to “remove the barriers and headaches from your ornamental steel projects” through a design-thinking approach that encourages creative freedom. The company emphasizes in-house control from concept to installation as its primary differentiator.
